hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks, pool party at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock to close July 6 for year-long $3 million renovation
cards.teaser: Stuart's public dock will close Sunday for renovations that will nearly double its capacity from 18 to 44 slips when the project is complete next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, the city is working to accommodate businesses that rely on the dock during the closure. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing his company to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock's non-floating section to continue boarding passengers. Kuyrkendall said modernizing and expanding the dock will be great for the city and his business.

cards.headline: Four Martin County teens arrested after 14-year-old robbed at gunpoint
cards.teaser: Four teenagers were arrested in Martin County Thursday after robbing a 14-year-old boy at gunpoint.
cards.body:
Four teenagers were arrested in Martin County Thursday after robbing a 14-year-old boy at gunpoint. The incident led to multiple arrests as law enforcement responded to the armed robbery.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office took the four teens into custody following the robbery of the juvenile victim. The suspects targeted the 14-year-old in what authorities described as a gunpoint robbery.

The arrests came after the reported armed robbery Thursday in Martin County. Law enforcement officials responded to the incident and apprehended the four teenage suspects.

The four teens now face charges related to the armed robbery of the 14-year-old victim. The Martin County Sheriff's Office continues to handle the case involving the juvenile suspects and victim.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock to close Sunday for $3 million renovation, nearly doubling boat slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will shut down on July 6 for a major renovation expected to wrap up by next Fourth of July. The $3 million project will significantly expand the facility's capacity, increasing available boat slips from 18 to 44 to accommodate both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation is being funded through a state grant and transportation impact fees. The work will include construction of a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. With over 1,400 boaters relying on the dock annually, city officials say the improvements are essential for the community's future.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed emphasized that the upgrades serve multiple purposes beyond simply adding more spaces. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it." The enhanced design and structure should better protect the facility and vessels during severe weather events, a critical consideration for a waterfront community.

Businesses that operate from the dock have worked with the city to develop solutions for continuing their operations during the closure. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which depends on the dock for passenger boarding and drop-off, expressed initial concerns about the yearlong shutdown. However, city officials found a compromise that allows the business to remain functional. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, explained the arrangement: "So they're allowing us to build a gate right here at the end of the downtown Stuart dock. This is the non-floating section, but still we're going to be able to open this up and board people right here." Kuyrkendall stressed the importance of the dock to Stuart's identity and economy, stating "Stuart is not Stuart without the water."

Local boat captain Parker Fisher, who operates from Stuart, supports the project. "It's definitely needed some work over the years, so I'm glad they're putting money into it," Fisher said. Kuyrkendall acknowledged the dock's current crowding issues, particularly during weekends when available spots become scarce. He sees the modernization as beneficial for both the city and the businesses that depend on the facility. "Modernizing and expanding this back dock is really going to be great for the city but also for us as well," Kuyrkendall said.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds and Ashley Moody form unified ticket for Florida Governor and U.S. Senate races
cards.body:
Byron Donalds and Ashley Moody are coordinating their campaigns for Florida Governor and U.S. Senate, announcing joint appearances, mutual endorsements, and grassroots events designed to consolidate Republican support ahead of the November General Election. Moody endorsed Donalds, saying "He is a proven conservative leader who will fight to make Florida safer, healthier, and more affordable as Governor." She noted their shared work in Tallahassee and Washington on tax cuts, immigration enforcement, and prescription drug costs. Donalds reciprocated the endorsement, stating "Her proven leadership as Attorney General and now as a United States Senator makes her the right choice to continue serving our state." The campaigns plan to emphasize public safety, education, economic growth, and senior issues while contrasting themselves with the Democratic field.

Donalds, who represents Naples in Congress, entered the gubernatorial race in early 2025 with backing from former President Donald Trump. His campaign raised a record 22.2 million dollars in the first quarter for a non-incumbent Florida gubernatorial candidate and has now exceeded 67 million dollars overall. He has qualified for the ballot and secured endorsements from the Florida Farm Bureau's FarmPAC and legislative leaders. A former state Representative with a finance background, Donalds would become Florida's first Black Governor if elected. He faces primary opposition from Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, former House Speaker Paul Renner, and businessman James Fishback, though Trump's endorsement and fundraising strength have positioned him as the frontrunner.

Moody, a fifth-generation Floridian and former federal prosecutor and Hillsborough Circuit Judge, served six years as Attorney General before Ron DeSantis appointed her to the U.S. Senate seat vacated by Marco Rubio, who became Secretary of State. During her time as Attorney General, she helped secure billions in opioid settlements for Florida. She was sworn in on January 21, 2025, has received Trump's endorsement, and has qualified for the Special Election to complete the remaining two years of Rubio's term.

On the Democratic side, former Republican Congressman David Jolly leads the gubernatorial field with former U.S. Representative Gwen Graham as his running mate. The Democratic Senate race remains uncertain after teacher Josh Weil withdrew due to a medical issue. The Primary Election is scheduled for Tuesday, August 18, with voter registration closing July 20. The General Election will follow on Tuesday, November 3, with registration closing October 5.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie advances plan for Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie is moving forward with a partial interchange project on Florida's Turnpike at Midway Road to improve accessibility and support the city's continued growth. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance authorizing the transfer of 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to facilitate the interchange construction. The city council will hold a final vote on the land donation at a future meeting.

The new interchange is intended to address a significant gap in Turnpike access currently affecting Port St. Lucie residents. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for the city, explained that the project serves a dual purpose: accommodating growth that has already happened while preparing for anticipated development over the next two to five decades. The partial interchange represents part of a larger effort by FDOT to improve regional transportation, including the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project designed to reduce congestion and enhance safety in the area.

Work is underway on the first phase of the Midway Road widening initiative, which will expand the roadway from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, stretching from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design stage with construction expected to commence in Summer 2027. The partial Turnpike interchange is also still in design phase. Along with the road expansion, FDOT is planning to construct bike and pedestrian paths plus sidewalks throughout the project corridor.

Local residents acknowledge both the challenges and benefits of the ongoing construction. Port St. Lucie resident Erin Scheumeister noted that while the work can be disruptive, she recognizes its necessity for the community. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," Scheumeister said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." As the project progresses through its various phases over the coming years, residents can expect continued improvements to regional connectivity and safety along this key transportation corridor.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit company proposes elevated network from West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
California-based autonomous transit company Glydways is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The system would also connect the convention center, nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Glydways will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could potentially come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. The company also said the system would be priced like public transit rather than private rideshare and would require local employees for operations centers and maintenance facilities. Tuesday's meeting is expected to determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal rather than approve construction.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County zoning board recommends denying Project Tango data center near Arden
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny a proposed hyperscale AI data center near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

One of the central issues during Thursday's hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. The board's recommendation comes just days after Palm Beach County planning staff recommended approval of the project. Project developer Ernie Cox said he was disappointed by the board's recommendation but plans to use the feedback from Thursday's hearing to strengthen his case before county commissioners. Cox said his team will review the issues raised during the hearing and provide additional information before the July 15 meeting.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets roof repaired, lien removed after WPTV investigates
cards.teaser: Lantana homeowner Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran, saw a nearly $7,000 lien lifted from his home within hours after WPTV contacted the roofing contractor he said left work unfinished.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, received relief after WPTV stepped in to help resolve issues with a roofing contractor. McCoy hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. He made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company but said two holes were left unfinished on the back side of his home. McCoy said the company stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails beginning in January. Letters from Gulfeagle Supply then arrived warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien with the county on his home. The lien document stated that Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid for those supplies.

After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke directly with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing about the unpaid materials and lien, a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized arrived within an hour. McCoy also learned the contractor would send someone back to fix the two unfinished areas on his roof. About an hour after receiving the waiver, McCoy sent WPTV a photo of crews back on his roof finishing the job.

cards.headline: Delray Beach golf training center delayed three months, costs $90,000 after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box near Delray Beach, said contractor problems delayed his virtual golf training center by three months and cost approximately $90,000 in repairs and double payments.
cards.body:
Tom Molen's dream of opening Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, became costly when contractor problems delayed the project by three months. Instead of opening in April as scheduled, Molen said the licensed contractor's work had to be redone, costing approximately $90,000. The delays also triggered what Molen called a "double pay" situation on multiple services. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," he said. That estimate does not account for lost revenue during the delays or the expense of hiring another contractor to fix the problems.

Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, the organization Molen worked with, is warning property and business owners to thoroughly vet contractors before hiring them. Founder David Allan estimates that 25% to 35% of homeowners and property owners in Palm Beach County face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. The most common contractor complaints in the county involve roofing, windows and air conditioning work. Despite the setbacks, Tee Box is preparing for its grand opening on July 17.

hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council has taken the first step toward a major transportation improvement by approving an ordinance to donate 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation. The land will support the construction of a partial interchange on the Florida Turnpike, a project designed to enhance accessibility for residents and visitors as the city continues expanding. City council will hold a final vote on the land donation at a future meeting.

The new interchange addresses a critical transportation challenge in the area. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, there is currently a significant gap between entrances and exits to the Turnpike within city limits. The interchange project is part of a broader strategy to accommodate both the growth that has already happened and the anticipated expansion over the next two to five decades. FDOT is working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding the partial interchange to better serve the community's transportation needs.

The interchange project is part of the larger $95 million Midway Road Widening Project, which focuses on reducing congestion and improving safety. Currently, construction crews are working on the first phase of road widening, expanding the roadway from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, which will widen the road from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial interchange for the Turnpike is also still in the design phase. Beyond the road widening work, FDOT plans to add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks as part of the overall project.

Local residents recognize both the inconvenience and necessity of the construction work. While some neighbors acknowledge that ongoing construction can be disruptive, they understand the improvements are needed. One resident noted that the expanded road capacity will make commuting easier and more accessible. The Midway Road Widening Project represents a significant investment in Port St. Lucie's infrastructure as the city works to keep pace with its growing population and improve traffic flow throughout the region.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Marine Unit rescues two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1, thanks to a quick response from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit and their decision to wear life jackets. The Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded, showing both occupants in the water after their boat went down.

The boaters were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post, "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life. We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets roof fixed, lien removed after WPTV intervenes with Boynton Beach contractor

When WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, he declined to comment on camera. McCoy also learned the contractor would return to fix the two problem areas on his roof. About an hour after receiving the waiver, McCoy sent WPTV a photo showing crews back on his roof completing the work.

cards.headline: Delray Beach area golf training center Tee Box delayed 3 months, costs $90,000 after contractor problems
cards.teaser: What started as a dream business built around a love for golf quickly turned into months of frustration, repairs and financial setbacks for one Palm Beach County entrepreneur opening Tee Box near Delray Beach.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, faced significant delays and costs due to contractor problems. The project was delayed three months from its scheduled April opening after the hired contractor repeatedly postponed work. Even though the contractor was licensed, Molen said the work ultimately had to be redone, creating a costly domino effect. Molen estimated the issues cost him $90,000, not including lost revenue during delays or the expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," Molen explained.

David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, estimates 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. Despite the setbacks, Molen remains focused on moving forward. The grand opening for Tee Box is set for July 17.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach could consider elevated autonomous transit network connecting downtown to airport
cards.teaser: A California-based autonomous transit company is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to the airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present an elevated self-driving vehicle network proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday. The system would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the downtown-to-airport trip to less than 10 minutes. The company estimates seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

The company describes the system as a modern alternative to light rail, streetcars and people movers. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said it functions like a "horizontal elevator," bypassing traffic congestion entirely. He noted increasing congestion along Okeechobee Boulevard, Southern Boulevard and Belvedere Road as evidence the region needs new transportation solutions. While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of traditional light rail, which carries South Florida estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal rather than approve construction.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
hero.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at the Turnpike.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city. He said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website for the project, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

According to the FDOT website, the partial interchange is still in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths, along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies and life jackets that kept them afloat.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post that the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call," the post stated.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation to nearly double boat slip capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses and boaters who rely on the dock for drop-off and pick-up. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will continue running during construction. The city is allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock on the non-floating section. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said modernizing and expanding the dock will be great for the city and for the business.

cards.headline: Delray Beach golf training center Tee Box delayed three months, costs owner $90,000 after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen's Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center on Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, was delayed from its April opening to July after problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center on Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard near Delray Beach, said his project was delayed by three months after problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space. Instead of opening on schedule in April, the project was constantly pushed off, Molen said. Even though the contractor was licensed, the work ultimately had to be redone, creating a costly domino effect that Molen estimates cost him $90,000. That estimate does not include the revenue lost during the delays or the added expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," Molen explained.

Molen worked with Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, which is warning property and business owners to thoroughly vet contractors before hiring them. David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, estimates 25 percent to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have the proper licenses and insurance before any work begins. After months of delays and repairs, Tee Box is preparing for its grand opening set for July 17.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran's roof repairs completed, lien removed after WPTV steps in
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, came to WPTV's Let's Hear It event in Boynton Beach after months of frustration with a roofing contractor that left him with unfinished repairs and a lien on his home.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. McCoy made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000. While mostly satisfied with the work, McCoy said the contractor left two holes unfinished on the back of his home and stopped responding to his requests for completion. Screenshots McCoy shared with WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey showed that between January 10 and May, he called, texted and emailed the company multiple times. A worker responded on February 5, saying the owner would call him, but McCoy said the owner never did.

McCoy then received letters from Gulfeagle Supply warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien against his home. The lien document stated Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid. After Hussey spoke with the Seabreeze Roofing owner about the unpaid materials and lien, the owner declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien, signed and notarized by Gulfeagle Supply. About an hour after receiving the waiver, McCoy sent WPTV a photo showing crews back on his roof finishing the remaining work.

cards.headline: Martin County opens portal in August for mobile home repair funding under new Florida law
cards.teaser: Senate Bill 594 opens up $167 million in state affordable housing funding to help mobile and manufactured home owners pay for emergency repairs and storm-hardening retrofits. The law took effect July 1.
cards.body:
Nearly 140 new Florida laws took effect July 1st, including Senate Bill 594, which makes $167 million in state affordable housing funding available to mobile and manufactured home owners for emergency repairs and storm-hardening improvements. The legislation followed an investigation into Florida's aging housing stock after an EF-3 tornado destroyed 138 homes at Spanish Lakes Country Club Community in Fort Pierce and killed six people. The investigation revealed that nearly 700,000 mobile and manufactured homes in Florida, roughly two-thirds of the state's more than 1 million such homes, were built before current federal safety standards and cannot withstand modern storms.

Martin County Human Services will open an online portal in August to accept applications. According to Julie Stellatos with the county agency, approximately 75 percent of Martin County's annual SHIP funding, typically between $1 million and $1.5 million, can now be directed toward eligible mobile and manufactured homeowners. Applications can be completed online or requested by phone to be mailed. Stellatos emphasizes that since funding operates on a first-come, first-served basis, applicants should gather paperwork quickly. Prospective applicants can visit the Florida Housing Finance Corporation website to locate their county or city and find information about available funding amounts, income eligibility requirements, and contact information.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks, pool party at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds and Ashley Moody form unified ticket for Florida Governor and U.S. Senate races
hero.body:
Byron Donalds and Ashley Moody are coordinating their campaigns for Florida Governor and U.S. Senate, announcing joint appearances, mutual endorsements, and grassroots events designed to consolidate Republican support ahead of the November General Election. Moody endorsed Donalds, saying "He is a proven conservative leader who will fight to make Florida safer, healthier, and more affordable as Governor." She noted their shared work in Tallahassee and Washington on tax cuts, immigration enforcement, and prescription drug costs. Donalds reciprocated the endorsement, stating "Her proven leadership as Attorney General and now as a United States Senator makes her the right choice to continue serving our state." The campaigns plan to emphasize public safety, education, economic growth, and senior issues while contrasting themselves with the Democratic field.

Donalds, who represents Naples in Congress, entered the gubernatorial race in early 2025 with backing from former President Donald Trump. His campaign raised a record 22.2 million dollars in the first quarter for a non-incumbent Florida gubernatorial candidate and has now exceeded 67 million dollars overall. He has qualified for the ballot and secured endorsements from the Florida Farm Bureau's FarmPAC and legislative leaders. A former state Representative with a finance background, Donalds would become Florida's first Black Governor if elected. He faces primary opposition from Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, former House Speaker Paul Renner, and businessman James Fishback, though Trump's endorsement and fundraising strength have positioned him as the frontrunner.

Moody, a fifth-generation Floridian and former federal prosecutor and Hillsborough Circuit Judge, served six years as Attorney General before Ron DeSantis appointed her to the U.S. Senate seat vacated by Marco Rubio, who became Secretary of State. During her time as Attorney General, she helped secure billions in opioid settlements for Florida. She was sworn in on January 21, 2025, has received Trump's endorsement, and has qualified for the Special Election to complete the remaining two years of Rubio's term.

On the Democratic side, former Republican Congressman David Jolly leads the gubernatorial field with former U.S. Representative Gwen Graham as his running mate. The Democratic Senate race remains uncertain after teacher Josh Weil withdrew due to a medical issue. The Primary Election is scheduled for Tuesday, August 18, with voter registration closing July 20. The General Election will follow on Tuesday, November 3, with registration closing October 5.

cards.headline: Florida showcases state history at Washington pavilion during nation's 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Florida is drawing thousands of visitors to its pavilion at the Great American State Fair in Washington as the nation marks its 250th anniversary, with the state's tourism chief reporting more than 9,000 visitors in a single day.
cards.body:
Florida is showcasing its history and culture at the Great American State Fair in Washington, D.C., during the nation's 250th anniversary celebration. The Florida pavilion, a 30-foot-by-30-foot space developed through collaboration between the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Florida Department of State, and Florida Fish and Wildlife Commission, features fact boards celebrating entertainers like Tom Petty and Jimmy Buffett and literary figures including Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings and Marjorie Stoneman Douglas. Video walls create immersive experiences of underwater manatee habitats and orange groves, while children can play putt-putt golf on a green shaped like Florida. According to Bryan Griffin, President and CEO of VISIT FLORIDA, the pavilion attracted more than 9,000 visitors in a single day after opening. Giveaways including Florida panther stickers and free manatee plushies have drawn crowds, and the pavilion will raffle off a St. Augustine vacation. The fair remains open through July 10.

Florida House on Capitol Hill will host open house events on July 3 and 4 starting at 10 a.m., offering free orange juice and Gatorade to visitors. Founded in 1973 by an act of the Florida Legislature, the facility currently features its "Legacy of Launch" exhibit exploring 75 years of aerospace activity in Florida, from the early Mercury missions to recent Artemis launches. According to Ethan Leckie, Communications and Events Coordinator, the exhibit highlights Florida's significant contributions to the nation's space program.

cards.headline: Florida airports expected to see smaller July 4 travel increases compared to other major U.S. cities
cards.teaser: Jacksonville International Airport will lead Florida metro areas with a 13.2% increase in arriving flights during the Independence Day holiday, but Florida airports lag behind most major U.S. cities in projected travel growth.
cards.body:
Researchers with Luxury Link projected that Florida's major airports will see smaller increases in arriving flights during the Independence Day holiday stretch compared to most other major U.S. cities. Jacksonville International Airport ranked 43rd nationally for flight increases, the highest ranking among 51 metropolitan areas analyzed. The First Coast metropolis will experience a 13.2% increase in arriving flights, averaging 93.3 incoming aircraft per day during the holiday period, up from a normal average of 82.4 arriving flights. Tampa ranked 46th with a projected 12.2% increase, accounting for 265.4 daily arrivals compared to the usual 236.4. Orlando followed at 48th with an 11.1% projected bump, while Miami ranked 50th.

The increases at Florida airports pale compared to top-ranking metro areas nationwide. Seattle led the study with arriving flights projected to increase by 28.1%, followed by Portland with a 25.3% increase and Fresno, California, with a 23% uptick. Luxury Link concluded that the Fourth of July represents one of the most significant travel periods of the year, combining a major national holiday with peak summer vacation season. The surge in travel activity, however, comes with downsides. Across the country, the study projected cancellations to jump by 121.5% and delays lasting more than three hours to spike by 74.6%.

cards.headline: Florida Fish and Wildlife urges residents to leave fireworks to professionals to protect nesting sea turtles
cards.teaser: The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is warning Fourth of July beachgoers that personal fireworks can disorient nesting sea turtles and shorebirds during peak nesting season.
cards.body:
As Florida's coastlines prepare for a surge of Fourth of July weekend visitors, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is urging beachgoers to protect nesting sea turtles and shorebirds. The state's beaches are critical nesting grounds for sea turtles and gathering places for shorebirds, many of which are especially vulnerable during peak nesting season. While municipal fireworks displays will light up the sky across Florida, the FWC warns that personal fireworks can startle and disrupt wildlife. "The loud sounds and bright lights of personal fireworks on beaches and adjacent waterways can significantly disorient and disrupt nesting sea turtles and waterbirds, as well as their hatchlings and chicks," an FWC news release said.

FWC officials stress the importance of cleaning up after a day at the beach by removing all trash, filling in holes dug in the sand, and taking home toys or beach furniture before nightfall. Obstacles on the beach can prevent sea turtles from nesting and prevent hatchlings from reaching the water once they emerge from their nests, while also entangling shorebirds, turtles and other wildlife. For those living near the beach, officials recommend turning off or dimming lights at night, as artificial lighting along the shoreline is a major hazard for nesting sea turtles. Lights on or near the beach can misdirect turtles and hatchlings away from the ocean toward potential danger.

cards.headline: Florida Senate Democratic Leader Lori Berman endorses Alex Vindman for U.S. Senate
cards.teaser: Florida Senate Democratic Leader Lori Berman of Delray Beach is endorsing Alex Vindman as he runs for U.S. Senate, citing his commitment to defending women's rights and reproductive freedom.
cards.body:
Florida Senate Democratic Leader Lori Berman of Delray Beach endorsed Alex Vindman for U.S. Senate, citing women's rights and reproductive freedom as central issues. "Women's rights and reproductive freedom are on the ballot, and we need leaders who will never back down from defending them," Berman said. "Alex Vindman understands what's at stake and will fight to protect a woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions, not have those decisions made by politicians."

Vindman is challenging U.S. Senator Ashley Moody, a Plant City Republican. Berman's support comes as Vindman competes against state Rep. Angie Nixon, a Jacksonville Democrat, in an Aug. 18 primary. The endorsement was announced the same week Vindman announced key union endorsements and raised another $8.5 million in the second quarter for his campaign. "As a father of a 15-year-old daughter, I am running to make sure young people like my daughter have the opportunities and freedoms they need to thrive in Florida," Vindman said. Vindman gained national prominence after providing key testimony to Congress that led to the first impeachment of President Donald Trump. His campaign released a memo this week arguing a potential path to victory exists due to a strong anti-Trump political environment, despite Florida's rightward shift in voter registrations.

cards.headline: Florida Clerks of Court highlight jury service role during nation's 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Florida's 67 Clerks of Court are conducting a public awareness campaign reminding residents that trial by jury was a central principle for which the nation's founders fought.
cards.body:
Florida Court Clerks and Comptrollers are commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary by highlighting their oversight of jury services. As the nation celebrates 250 years of independence, the right to trial by jury stands as one of the central tenets for which our founders fought, said FCCC President and Marion County Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller Gregory C. Jury service remains one of the most important duties entrusted to citizens. The 67 Florida Clerks of Court are engaged in a public awareness campaign this year reminding residents of the important role that courts play in ensuring the constitutional promise of equal protection under the law.

Court services were among the chief concerns by American colonists, as demonstrated by the Declaration of Independence's accusation that King George III was "depriving us in many cases of the benefits of trial by jury." That ideal is enshrined in the Sixth Amendment of the U.S. Constitution. While Clerks of Court maintain courthouses to ensure fair trials, they also oversee the complex task of assembling juries, which consist of registered voters. This involves summoning qualified jurors, overseeing jury selection, administering information and assistance to jurors, managing juror attendance and compensation, and monitoring jury selection to ensure fairness and efficiency.

cards.headline: Independent candidate Mike Klein to formally announce congressional bid at Gainesville concert
cards.teaser: Independent congressional candidate Mike Klein will formally kick off his campaign Saturday with a public concert at Bo Diddley Plaza in downtown Gainesville celebrating America's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
Independent congressional candidate Mike Klein will formally launch his campaign Saturday at the "Defending Democracy" Independence Day concert, running from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. at Bo Diddley Plaza in downtown Gainesville. The event will feature live music, speakers, voter registration efforts and food trucks. Creative Vibes, a Gainesville-based funk, R&B and soul band led by the grandson of legendary musician Bo Diddley, will perform alongside the Thomas Allain Band, another Gainesville group serving as the main act. According to Klein's campaign, the event will honor the rights won by generations of Americans and promote the duty of citizens to defend democracy and renew a government that belongs to its people.

A Desert Storm veteran, Klein serves as Chair of Warrior Centric Health, a nonprofit advocating for veteran healthcare. He is running on a populist platform focused on campaign finance reform, affordability and avoiding unnecessary wars. "Florida's 3rd Congressional District deserves a representative free from party bosses, corporate donors, and foreign interests," Klein said. As an independent, Klein faces significant obstacles in a district where 61% of voters reelected U.S. Representative Kat Cammack to a third term in 2024. The seat is rated Solid R with a Partisan Voter Index of R+10. The district stretches west from Ocala to the Gulf and north to the Georgia border. Democrats Troy Albers, Seth Harp, George Hubac and Tom Wells are also running.

hero.headline: Stuart downtown dock to close Monday for $3 million renovation, will nearly double slip capacity
hero.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will shut down July 6 for a $3 million renovation expected to wrap up by next Fourth of July. The project will significantly expand the facility's capacity, nearly doubling the number of available slips from 18 to 44 for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The upgrades are funded through a state grant and transportation impact fees.

The renovation work will add a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. According to Stuart Mayor Sean Reed, these improvements serve a critical purpose beyond just adding space. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it." With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, the project represents a significant investment in the community's waterfront infrastructure.

The dock's closure has raised concerns for businesses that depend on the facility. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates tours from the dock, initially worried about continuing operations during construction. However, the city found a solution. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for the company, explained the arrangement: "They're allowing us to build a gate right here at the end of the downtown Stuart dock. This is the non-floating section, but still we're going to be able to open this up and board people right here." This accommodation will allow the tour company to continue serving customers during the renovation period.

Kuyrkendall emphasized the dock's importance to Stuart's identity and economy. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," he said. He also noted the current limitations, especially during peak times. "On the weekend that's when it can get a little hectic at the dock and you know it's never great for us when we're squeezing in and trying to find spots." Boat captain Parker Fisher, who operates in Stuart, supports the improvements. "It's definitely needed some work over the years, so I'm glad they're putting money into it," Fisher said. Kuyrkendall shared this optimism about the modernization project, saying the expanded dock will benefit both the city and local businesses like his own.

cards.headline: Woman dies after being pulled from burning home in Hobe Sound
cards.teaser: A woman died after being pulled from a burning home in Hobe Sound on Thursday.
cards.body:
A woman died after being pulled from a burning home in Hobe Sound on Thursday.

The incident occurred in Hobe Sound, a community in Martin County. No further information about the circumstances of the fire has been released.

cards.headline: Four Martin County teens arrested after 14-year-old robbed at gunpoint
cards.teaser: Four teenagers in Martin County were arrested after a 14-year-old was robbed at gunpoint.
cards.body:
Four teenagers in Martin County were arrested after a 14-year-old was robbed at gunpoint. The arrests followed an alleged robbery that led to a chase with Martin County deputies.

Martin County sheriff's officials discussed the armed robbery of the boy. The incident remains under investigation by the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances Midway Road widening and Florida Turnpike interchange project
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on the Florida Turnpike.

The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Florida Turnpike. FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. cards.headline: Palm Beach County Zoning Commission recommends denial of data center near Arden and Saddle View Elementary
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddle View Elementary School. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

One of the central issues during Thursday's hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Board members said they were not presented with enough evidence to conclude the facility would meet that standard. Project developer Ernie Cox said he was disappointed by the board's recommendation but plans to use the feedback from Thursday's hearing to strengthen his case before county commissioners.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit company proposes elevated network connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles to connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, along with the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. The company will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, bypassing traffic congestion entirely. The trip between downtown and the airport could take less than 10 minutes, with travel times estimated at seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. He referenced previous South Florida light rail discussions with estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Gettinger emphasized the service would be priced like public transit, not private rideshare. Tuesday's County Commission meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal, potentially leading to competing bids and deeper discussions on routes, station locations and financing.

Code Pro founder David Allan estimates 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. Despite the setbacks, Tee Box is preparing for its grand opening on July 17.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward on Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie is advancing a major transportation initiative that will widen Midway Road and create a partial interchange connecting to Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of city land to the Florida Department of Transportation. This land donation will support the development of the new interchange, which city officials say is needed to address a significant gap in current Turnpike access points throughout the city.

The $95 million Midway Road Widening Project aims to reduce congestion and improve safety along this critical corridor. Currently, crews are focused on the first phase of construction, which involves expanding the roadway from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, extending from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design stage with construction expected to start in summer 2027, according to the FDOT project website. Beyond widening the road surface, the project also includes improvements to the Turnpike bridge and will incorporate bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks.

Scott Samples, the strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, emphasized that the new interchange addresses both current needs and future growth. "There's a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie," Samples said. He added that the project is designed to "accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years." The partial interchange remains in the design phase, and the city council will vote on final approval of the land transfer at an upcoming meeting.

While construction activities have drawn attention from residents in the area, many recognize the project's importance. One nearby resident noted that the ongoing construction can be disruptive but acknowledged its necessity. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," she said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." As Port St. Lucie continues to grow, these infrastructure improvements represent a significant investment in the city's transportation network to support both current residents and future development.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters were safely rescued Wednesday after their small motorized boat took on water and sank in the Intracoastal Waterway. Both wore life jackets that kept them afloat until help arrived.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1 in the Intracoastal Waterway. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office noted that the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life and expressed gratitude that the call ended safely and pride in the swift response by Marine Unit deputies.

cards.headline: Body of missing diver found near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: Deputies recovered the body of a missing diver on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office reported finding the body of a missing diver near Fort Pierce Inlet on the Florida coast. The discovery was made Friday morning.

No additional details about the diver's identity or the circumstances surrounding the incident were immediately available from the sheriff's office.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested on child pornography charges
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce man faces child pornography charges following an arrest by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a Fort Pierce man on child pornography charges Thursday. The arrest followed an investigation by sheriff's deputies.

The charges were filed after evidence was gathered during the investigation. The sheriff's office has not released additional details about the case.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce officer works to help homeless find hope after lifetime of service
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce police officer is using his experience to assist homeless residents in the community.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce police officer is dedicating his efforts to helping homeless individuals in the city find hope and support. The officer has spent a lifetime in service and is now focusing on addressing homelessness in Fort Pierce.

The officer's work involves connecting homeless residents with resources and services. His efforts represent a community-focused approach to addressing homelessness in the Fort Pierce area.

cards.headline: St. Lucie scanner Facebook page distances itself from founder after Orbeez arrest
cards.teaser: A popular St. Lucie County scanner Facebook page has separated itself from its founder following an arrest related to Orbeez.
cards.body:
A St. Lucie County scanner Facebook page that reports local police and emergency activity has publicly distanced itself from its founder. The move came after the founder was arrested on charges related to Orbeez.

The page administrators announced the separation from the founder Thursday. The scanner page, which provides updates on local law enforcement activity to St. Lucie County residents, stated it is moving forward under new leadership.

cards.headline: Florida black bear sightings reported in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Residents in St. Lucie, Martin and Indian River counties have reported Florida black bear sightings.
cards.body:
Florida black bear sightings have been reported across St. Lucie County and neighboring Martin and Indian River counties. The reports came in Thursday from residents who spotted the bears in local areas.

Black bears are native to Florida and occasionally move through residential areas in search of food and habitat. The sightings reflect the ongoing presence of black bears in the Treasure Coast region.

hero.headline: Indian River Lagoon Council audit finds nearly $300,000 in questioned costs
hero.body:
An audit of the Indian River Lagoon Council has identified nearly $300,000 in questioned costs, according to Central Florida Public Media. The audit raises concerns about how the regional environmental organization has been managing public funds allocated for lagoon restoration and protection efforts.

The Indian River Lagoon Council coordinates environmental restoration efforts across multiple counties including Indian River County. The lagoon system stretches along Florida's east coast and has faced ongoing challenges including algae blooms, seagrass loss, and water quality degradation.

The questioned costs identified in the audit could affect future funding and operations of lagoon restoration projects in the region. The audit findings come as the lagoon continues to face environmental pressures from development and pollution.

Details about the specific nature of the questioned costs and what corrective actions may be required have not been disclosed in the initial report. The council will need to address the audit findings to maintain its standing with state and federal funding agencies.

cards.headline: SERHANT real estate brand enters Vero Beach market
cards.teaser: SERHANT has joined other major real estate brands operating in Vero Beach, adding to the competitive market in Indian River County.
cards.body:
SERHANT has established a presence in the Vero Beach real estate market, joining other major real estate brands already operating in the area. The expansion reflects continued activity in Indian River County's property market.

Vero Beach has attracted multiple national and regional real estate firms in recent years. The market has remained active with buyers and sellers conducting transactions across residential and commercial properties.

SERHANT's entry into Vero Beach marks the latest expansion by a major real estate brand into the Indian River County market. The company will compete with established firms already serving local property buyers and sellers.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closing July 6 for $3 million renovation
cards.teaser: Stuart's public dock will close Sunday for a year-long $3 million renovation that will nearly double slip capacity from 18 to 44 slips.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project expected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses that rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be allowed to build a gate at the non-floating section of the downtown Stuart dock to continue boarding passengers. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the solution will enable the company to continue running during construction. Boat captain Parker Fisher, who is based in Stuart, supports the project, saying the dock has needed work over the years.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances Florida Turnpike interchange, Midway Road expansion
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres to FDOT for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike as part of the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. According to Samples, the interchange addresses accessibility and is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial interchange is also still in the design phase. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County zoning board recommends denial of data center near Arden
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted to recommend denial of Project Tango, a proposed AI data center near Arden and Saddle View Elementary School.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddle View Elementary School.

One of the central issues during Thursday's hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Residents raised concerns about potential health, safety, environmental and noise impacts. Project developer Ernie Cox said he was disappointed by the board's recommendation but plans to use the feedback to strengthen his case before county commissioners. The Palm Beach County Commission will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed, roof fixed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, had a nearly $7,000 lien removed from his home after WPTV intervened with his roofing contractor.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, sought help from WPTV after months of frustration with Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach. McCoy hired the company to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season and made six payments totaling more than $17,000. After completing most of the work, the company left two holes unfinished on the back side of his home and stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails starting in January. McCoy said he visited the company's building two or three times and received only one response, on February 5, when a worker promised the owner would call him, but never did.

The situation worsened when letters from Gulfeagle Supply arrived warning that a nearly $7,000 lien had been filed on his home. The lien stated that Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid. WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, who declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons. Within an hour of that conversation, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized. McCoy also learned the contractor would return to finish the roof repairs, and about an hour after receiving the waiver, crews were back on his roof completing the work.

cards.headline: Delray Beach area golf training center delayed three months after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen's Tee Box virtual golf training center near Delray Beach was delayed three months and cost $90,000 extra after contractor problems forced repairs and rework.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, said his project was delayed three months after problems with a licensed contractor hired to prepare the space. Instead of opening in April as scheduled, the contractor constantly pushed off work and the job ultimately had to be redone, creating a costly domino effect. Molen estimates the issues cost $90,000, not including lost revenue or the expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. The repairs required double pay for electricians, HVAC technicians and drywall contractors.

David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, estimates that 25 percent to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners in Palm Beach County face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. Despite the setbacks, Molen said he is focused on moving forward. Tee Box is preparing for its grand opening set for July 17.
